subject: Architecture
title: Critical Regionalism: Building for Place
description: A quick, practical guide to Critical Regionalism: Building for Place.

hook.text: Critical regionalism argued that buildings should belong to their place, not look the same everywhere.

buildup.text: Architects used local materials, responded to climate, and respected cultural traditions.

discovery.text: Tadao Ando's Church of the Light in Japan uses a cross-shaped slit to let light form the altar.

twist.text: Globalization fought back — developers wanted brand-name 'starchitect' towers, not local designs.

climax.text: The movement influenced sustainable design by showing that climate-responsive buildings need less energy.

punchline.text: Build for the place, not the portfolio. Architecture's hardest lesson.

quiz.question: What is the core principle of critical regionalism?
options: Buildings should use only recycled materials
Buildings should respond to their specific place and climate
Buildings should reject all modern technology
